Nyirlovo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírlövő, Hungary

Not demolished. Nyírlövő's Jewish cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, with its newest tombstone dated 1921. Jews first appeared in the village in 1770; the population fluctuated over the following century - peaking at 70 in 1920 before falling to 37 by 1941, and just 8 families by mid-April 1944, when the community was deported via the Kisvárda Ghetto to Auschwitz. Only three survivors returned from forced labor after the war, and by the 1949 census just two Jews remained in the settlement.
